judgment.summary: Norb Studio's page runs and delivers a genuine real-time 3D experience: a full-screen WebGL hero sculpture that responds to pointer movement and clicks, a readable studio narrative with bold scroll transitions, a scroll-driven 3D helix gallery, and a 3D-treated contact form with strong hover/focus feedback. Desktop and 390x844 mobile layouts were usable. The main weakness is the loading cube, which was only observed through the accessibility snapshot (six faces reading N, R, O, B, S, ✦) and could not be captured in a delivered screenshot before it transitioned away, so the exact spin/letter delivery could not be fully verified visually.

runtime.reason: Page loaded successfully with title 'Norb Studio — Form Beyond the Familiar', a 1440x900 WebGL 2.0 canvas, and no blocking script errors. The only console entry was a favicon.ico 404; the full page, sections and 3D content rendered.

scene.reason: Valid real-time 3D is present across the page: the hero shows a glossy lime torus knot with orbital rings, glass spheres and floating primitives at distinct depths with occlusion and changing scale/color, and the work section shows a perspective helix of artwork panels. Runtime probing confirmed a WebGL 2.0 canvas and matrix3d helix transforms.

checks.reason: Genuine depth and geometry were inspected across multiple distinct views: three hero states (rest, pointer-enlarged, click-mutated), the studio's 3D orbital study, and three helix angles (180°, 302°, 680°). Occlusion, perspective, scale and material changes are visible; runtime probes confirmed WebGL and 3D matrix transforms.

Composition, materials, lighting, color and legibility were inspected. The page has a coherent editorial art-studio identity: oversized type, cream/black/coral/lime palette, glossy 3D materials and counter-rotating cards. The giant 'OBJECTS IN orbit.' title intentionally overlays part of the gallery and reduces legibility of some cards, a local visual tension rather than a failure.

Primary UI interactions produced meaningful scene feedback: pointer movement enlarged/distorted the hero sculpture, clicking changed it to a coral material/orientation, scrolling rotated the helix, and hovering the contact field turned it lime with a beveled treatment.

Repeat and reverse behavior worked. Scrolling forward advanced the helix readout from 180° to 302° to 680° with different cards facing the camera; scrolling back restored the 302° state and the same card arrangement. The contact nav jump also recovered to a fully rendered section after a transient blank transition frame.

Both 1440x900 and 390x844 layouts were inspected. Desktop showed the full contact form, and mobile showed filled fields, the project selector, the send button and the footer/back-to-top control without horizontal clipping. Reload returned to a working hero. Console had only a favicon 404; network/resource diagnostics were recorded. Blank transition frames were observed but were nonblocking.

The full-screen hero contains interactive floating abstract 3D shapes. Pointer movement visibly enlarged and distorted the central knot, and clicking mutated it to a coral material/orientation while satellite shapes continued drifting.

A loader was observed on first load with a percentage counter, repeated NORB STUDIO marquee and a six-face rotating cube whose faces read N, R, O, B, S and a star glyph; it then transitioned to the hero. However, no delivered screenshot captured the cube itself (screenshot calls waited for the post-load hero), so the spin and letter-to-face presentation could not be visually verified. The cube also does not spell the full 'Norb Studio' name across its faces.

The narrative section presents readable studio story and goals ('We make the unreal feel touchable', independent 3D art studio statement, point-of-view copy and studio stats) with bold typography and scroll-triggered reveal transitions. A transient blank frame was captured between sections, followed by the fully readable composition.

The gallery is a recognizable 3D helix: nine artwork cards sit on a vertical spiral with progressive Y-axis rotation and vertical offset, and the on-screen readout advanced 180° → 302° → 680° as I scrolled. Reversing scroll restored the 302° arrangement. Cards occlude and pass in front of each other in perspective.

The contact form has a clear 3D treatment (raised cream panel over a green block, sphere behind it). Hovering the name field changed it to bright lime with a tactile bevel; on mobile the focused textarea turned purple and showed entered sample text. Name, email, project type and message inputs were filled through the UI and remained usable.

instruction.reason: All five requested sections and main flows are present and coherent. The specific minor omission is the loader cube: it carries N, R, O, B, S and a star rather than spelling/conveying the full 'Norb Studio' name on its faces, and its spin could not be confirmed in a delivered screenshot.

spatial.reason: Shapes, spatial relations, lighting and materials consistently serve the brief. The hero knot, orbiting rings, floating primitives, studio orb and helix cards all show credible depth, occlusion, perspective and material variety across multiple tested views.

interaction.reason: Required and repeated flows work: hero hover/click, nav jumping, helix scroll and reverse, and form hover/focus/typing. Local issues are multi-second blank transition frames between sections and the un-captured loader, which reduce discoverability and certainty during transitions.

visual.reason: Composition, typography, color and 3D form a coherent art-studio expression. Local defects include the oversized 'OBJECTS IN orbit.' overlay obscuring parts of gallery cards and blank full-screen transition frames that temporarily remove all information.

stability.reason: The page remained usable across desktop, mobile, reload, repeated hero interaction and repeat/reverse gallery scrolling. The only console error was a favicon 404, and no crashes occurred. Multi-second blank transition frames are local nonblocking issues; mobile reload and network-request listing were not separately verified.

limitations: The loading cube could not be captured in a delivered screenshot: screenshot calls waited until the loader had transitioned to the hero. The loader was observed through the accessibility snapshot at 70%, showing faces N, R, O, B, S, ✦ and a repeated NORB STUDIO marquee; its actual spin cadence is therefore only partly verified.

The browser network-request listing was not called because the 40-call browser budget was reached. evidence/console.txt contains the auto-captured console entry (favicon.ico 404), and evidence/network.txt contains read-only HTTP resource checks; no other missing resources were observed.
Mobile page reload and form submission/backend delivery were not tested. Form submission beyond usable inputs is not part of the stated requirements.
Reverse scrolling was verified in the helix gallery but not separately captured for the narrative section.
A 390px viewport does not certify real touch hardware.
Audio quality and internal implementation details were not evaluated.

checks.reason: Three desktop observations show coherent swing-set geometry and neighborhood depth from slightly different camera positions. The foreground A-frame partially occludes the background path and houses, tree and house silhouettes shift with the camera, and cast shadows establish ground contact.

The composition uses amber sky, burnt-orange foliage, brown timber, cream house walls, and warm lantern light consistently. Faceted trees, angular terrain, simplified houses, and polygonal leaves form a coherent low-poly treatment with clear title hierarchy and readable supporting text.

The offered bottom-right control changes from Move to wander to Camera at rest when activated, pauses the gentle camera motion, and changes back after activation again. The effect is visible in the scene framing and confirmed by the control's updated accessible label.

Pause and resume were repeated successfully, including a keyboard Tab-and-Enter activation whose state changed from Camera at rest to Move to wander. A mobile reload restored the default active camera mode, the full scene, title, and control without a recovery failure.

The 1440x900 and 390x844 layouts both keep the title, primary subject, and lower-right camera control visible and usable. Reloads succeeded at mobile width and after returning to desktop. Console diagnostics show zero messages, errors, or warnings; the network log shows index, styles, main script, and Three.js resources at 200 or 304.

A clearly recognizable wooden swing set, including crossbar, A-frame supports, chains, and two seats, is the foreground focus within a cozy neighborhood of houses, picket fences, autumn trees, pumpkins, and leaf litter. Depth is supported by overlapping geometry and long cast shadows.

The page title and large visible heading are Autumn Joys. The amber and russet palette, faceted low-poly trees and terrain, simplified houses, and polygonal leaves all visibly express the requested warm autumn atmosphere.

At desktop width the swing set remains dominant while the path, houses, and supporting details stay legible. At 390x844 the swing remains recognizable and centered, the title and subtitle fit without clipping, and the camera control remains reachable at the bottom edge.

instruction.reason: All stated requirements are delivered coherently: a Three.js-backed 3D swing set, a cozy autumn neighborhood, the visible title Autumn Joys, a warm palette, and a low-poly aesthetic. Tested desktop, mobile, control, keyboard, and reload states preserve the brief.

spatial.reason: The swing set's timber members, chains, seats, and ground contacts are coherent at the scale shown. Foreground/background layering, perspective, shadows, and changing camera framing consistently communicate depth, while neighborhood elements remain subordinate to the main subject.

interaction.reason: The advertised camera-wander control is discoverable, labeled, and reversible. Mouse toggling and keyboard activation both work, the label and scene motion respond immediately, repeated toggles remain consistent, and reload restores a usable default state.

visual.reason: Typography, overlay placement, warm color hierarchy, and low-poly scene forms work as one coherent expression. The large serif title balances the dense scene without obstructing the swing, and the restrained UI details reinforce the cozy neighborhood mood at both viewport sizes.

stability.reason: Desktop, mobile, camera toggles, keyboard activation, and reloads all completed without layout loss or blocking behavior. The console log contains zero messages or errors, and all logged page resources loaded successfully with 200 or 304 responses.

limitations: The 390x844 viewport was emulated through browser resize; real touch hardware and device-specific rendering were not tested.
No audio or downloadable export feature was advertised or present, so those aspects were not assessed.

judgment.summary: Sunroom is a complete balcony sun-study app: it renders an orbitable furnished balcony with wall, railing, overhang, furniture and planters; updates solar position from sample location, date and compass orientation; scrubs daylight with clear sun/shade feedback; supports moving planters in two side-by-side top views; and exposes its simplified solar assumptions without location or API credentials. Desktop and 390x844 flows remained usable, reload/reset recovered the default state, and diagnostics were clean.

runtime.reason: The page opened and completed its 3D scene load, all tested controls responded, reload recovered the default Dubai study, and the saved console log contains 0 errors and 0 warnings. The saved network log shows the document, CSS, app and three.js modules returning 200 on first load and 304 on reload.

scene.reason: This is genuine interactive 3D rather than a static image: orbiting produced three distinct viewpoints with stable geometry, depth, occlusion and parallax. The furnished balcony has a solid side wall, railings, a projecting overhang, deck, seating, tables and visible planters, and daylight changes alter broad shaded areas and planter sun/shade indicators coherently.

checks.reason: Three orbit views show consistent balcony depth, railing occlusion, overhang placement and furniture/planter positions. Moving the camera produces real spatial changes rather than a fixed or unrelated canvas.

The warm editorial controls and muted furnished scene form a coherent composition. Solar readouts, arrangement status, direct-sun/shade legend, type hierarchy and plan thumbnails remain legible on desktop and the narrow layout.

The primary controls produced meaningful feedback: changing location/date/orientation changed coordinates, solar azimuth/elevation and sunrise/noon/sunset; scrubbing changed the 3D lighting and the 0-6 sun counts; dragging a top-view planter moved it and updated the scene.

Boundary and reverse behavior worked: End reached 5:26 PM with all six planters shaded, dragging back to 9:38 AM restored mixed sun states, A/B switching retained the same time and distinct arrangements, reload restored defaults, and Reset reported 'Plans reset'.

At 1440x900 and 390x844 the 3D scene, time scrubber, comparison cards, location/date/orientation controls and assumptions remained reachable. Tab navigation visibly focused the play control. Reload completed successfully; console.txt reports no messages/errors and network.txt shows successful asset loads. Real touch hardware was not available.

The furnished balcony clearly contains a solid side wall, railing and large overhang. Across orbit and daylight states, shaded floor regions and planter indicators change consistently with those structures, including full shading near sunset.

Sydney, 21 June 2026 and East orientation replaced Dubai/South and updated the displayed coordinates, sunrise/noon/sunset, compass view and solar position. Daylight scrubbing changed the sun/shade result, including 0 of 6 at sunset and 4/3 of 6 at 9:38 AM.

Arrangement A's planter was dragged from the upper-left area to the lower-right in top view. The plan thumbnail moved, the active 3D arrangement reflected the changed layout, and the per-planter sun/shade treatment remained inspectable at the fixed selected time.

Arrangements A and B are distinct and remain visible together in the comparison panel at the same selected time. At 9:38 AM A shows 4 of 6 in sun while B shows 3 of 6, with different planter positions; switching the 3D stage between A and B preserves both layouts and the shared time.

Six bundled sample locations are offered and the app opened immediately without a location prompt, API key or account. The visible model-assumptions disclosure states NOAA-style clear-sky geometry, standard UTC offsets without daylight saving, ignored refraction/weather/external obstructions, and canopy shade tracing.

instruction.reason: All stated requirements were delivered coherently in tested states: furnished shadow-casting balcony, editable solar context, daylight scrub, movable planters, two arrangements at one time, visible assumptions and bundled sample locations without credentials.

spatial.reason: Geometry, depth, occlusion, furniture scale and daylight shading consistently serve the balcony-placement task across three camera views and multiple solar states.

interaction.reason: The primary sequence is reliable and understandable: set context, scrub time, inspect the 3D scene, drag planters, switch arrangements and compare counts. Boundary, reverse, reset and reload recovery all behaved correctly with immediate visual feedback.

visual.reason: Composition, typography, warm color, solar-state transitions and plan thumbnails reinforce the purpose and remain readable. The responsive layout preserves the same hierarchy and useful comparison context.

stability.reason: Loads, repeated controls, reset and reload were stable; desktop and narrow layouts remained usable; no console warnings/errors appeared and all required assets loaded successfully.

limitations: Touch gestures and real mobile hardware were not tested; mobile assessment used a 390x844 viewport per the rubric.

Numerical solar accuracy and exact shadow projection were not independently validated against astronomy data; the assessment relies on visible coherence and the app's disclosed simplified assumptions.
No export or download control was advertised, so there was no exported image to open and inspect.

Consecutive close-ups show the gear teeth and balance-wheel spokes at different angles while the hands advance. Frame differencing of the gear areas produced substantially more change than the static dial background, confirming visible continuous movement rather than a static picture.

judgment.summary: Loop Garden is a polished, functional browser music studio with a clear four-track sequencer, strong 3D garden presentation, working playback/edit flows, and a usable local pattern library. The main observed defect is that muting Moss Drums did not change its exposed pressed state or the textual/3D sounding indication. The 40-call cap was reached before import/export, clear/restore confirmations, deletion completion, reload persistence, reduced-motion playback, and the full mobile grid could be exercised, so those aspects are reported as limited rather than inferred.

runtime.reason: The page loaded successfully at 1440x900, rendered its title and full studio UI, and remained interactive through playback, editing, pattern saving, renaming, and deletion confirmation. The network log shows the HTML, stylesheet, application scripts, Three.js modules, and geometry utilities all returned 200; only favicon.ico returned 404. The WebGL warning added during the read-only canvas probe was probe-induced and did not block the page.

scene.reason: The right panel is a genuine live WebGL2 canvas, not a static image. It presents a fixed-camera 3D garden with clear depth, occlusion, shadows, emissive materials, and four spatially separated instruments. The playhead and sounding-state changes are reflected by changing instrument-local illumination and status text across playback states.

checks.reason: The scene is a fixed-camera design, so no orbit was expected. Desktop screenshots across stopped, playing, paused, and stopped-again states show consistent 3D geometry and occlusion, while the playhead and instrument glows change. A read-only runtime probe confirmed a WebGL2 canvas at 380x581 backing dimensions.

The two-panel composition, serif/small-caps typography, restrained moss/green and warm track colors, and shadowed diorama form a coherent identity. Track names, step numbers, transport state, and the 3D scene remain legible and clearly grouped at desktop width.

Play, pause, resume, stop, mouse step editing, keyboard step editing, tempo changes, volume changes, save, and rename all produced visible state feedback. The playhead, status text, active-step highlighting, focus ring, dirty-state label, and 3D previews made the primary interactions understandable.

Repeat playback and pause/resume/stop recovery worked, and delete correctly opened a confirmation dialog. Deletion was not completed, and clear/restore-demo cancellation and confirmation plus post-edit reload recovery were not exercised, so full reverse/destructive-flow coverage is incomplete.

The main UI was inspected at 1440x900 and the 390x844 layout was captured with a modal open; the modal fit and its actions remained reachable. The primary mobile grid/transport and lower controls were not inspected after closing the modal, and no reload was performed. Console diagnostics found only a nonblocking favicon 404 plus the probe-induced WebGL warning; server logs show all application assets loaded successfully.

The initial UI exposes Moss Drums, Root Bass, Leaf Keys, and Petal Bells across 16 steps with percussion, bass, and melodic parts. Playback started only after pressing Play, immediately advanced the playhead, showed 'Audio live', and produced sounding-instrument feedback. Network logs show only same-origin application assets, with no account, microphone, or remote audio request. Audible quality itself could not be judged because the browser audio was not listenable.

Track names and step numbers are clear, the playhead is unmistakable, inactive/active steps differ visibly, and step buttons expose on/off through their accessible names. Mouse editing and keyboard ArrowRight plus Enter editing worked, and keyboard focus was clearly outlined. Touch hardware and tap-driven editing were not available to verify.

Tempo changed from 104 to 106 BPM during playback, the Moss Drums volume display changed from 86 to 40, and the playhead plus 3D previews continued to update. However, clicking Mute Moss Drums left the button with aria-pressed false and the status still announced 'Moss Drums + Leaf Keys' when the drum row was active. Solo and actual audible mute/gain behavior were not verified.

Pause retained the playhead at step 7 and displayed 'Position held'; Resume continued playback, and Stop returned the indicator and status to step 1. The destructive-pattern flow showed a clear confirmation dialog for deletion, but the specifically requested Clear and Restore demo confirmations were not opened or canceled/confirmed.

Repeated tempo increases during playback still showed a single advancing playhead and one continuous playback state at 106 BPM, with no visible second loop. Audio-clock scheduling, steady audible rhythm, and note-to-sound alignment cannot be verified from screenshots or a muted headless browser.

Stopping playback returned the textual and 3D state to 'Waiting for play' and no visible note activity remained. Background suspension, explicit resume from suspension, pattern switching, and page departure were not exercised; audible stuck-note behavior cannot be assessed without listening.

The library contained three named patterns on desktop: Morning Dew, Moonlit Moss, and Petal Parade. 'Save current' produced a saved confirmation, dirty state was visibly indicated before saving, and renaming Moonlit Moss to 'Moonlit Moss Renamed' succeeded. Delete opened a confirmation dialog but was not completed, and restoration after refresh was not verified.

Export JSON and Import JSON controls are present, and the library states that malformed imports are rejected before the current pattern is touched. No export was downloaded, no JSON was imported, and malformed tempo, track, or step-count validation was not exercised.

Textual playback status is present and informative, and a visible 'Calm motion' reduced-motion switch exists. The 390x844 capture showed a centered confirmation modal that fit the viewport, but the compact main grid, track names, and transport were not observable behind it, and reduced-motion playback feedback was not exercised.

instruction.reason: The core music-studio flow is delivered coherently: a four-track 16-step demo plays after a gesture, editing and transport work, tempo and volume respond, three named patterns are present, and save/rename workflows are visible. The mute control did not visibly engage, and important requested areas remained unverified at the call limit, preventing a full four.

spatial.reason: The fixed-camera 3D garden consistently serves the task: instruments are spatially distinct, depth and occlusion read clearly, lighting and materials are coherent, and note-related glows/status changes link the ensemble to the sequencer.

interaction.reason: Primary playback, pause/resume/stop, mouse and keyboard editing, tempo, volume, save, rename, and confirmation feedback are discoverable and responsive. The mute state issue and incomplete recovery/import-export coverage are meaningful local limitations, but the tested sequences otherwise remained reliable.

visual.reason: Composition, typography, color hierarchy, active-step indication, and the 3D diorama form a cohesive, polished expression that improves understanding of the rhythm. The pattern modal also preserves the visual language and remains readable.

stability.reason: The tested desktop flows were stable and repeated playback/editing operations did not crash or freeze. The application assets loaded successfully; favicon.ico was the only normal 404. Mobile was only observed with a modal, reload was not tested, and the WebGL console warning was introduced by the read-only context probe rather than the app.

limitations: Audio was not audible in the headless browser, so sound quality, actual mute/solo gain, audio-clock scheduling, and audible note alignment remain unverified.
Touch hardware was unavailable; only mouse and keyboard editing and a narrow-viewport modal capture were tested.

judgment.summary: The submission is a polished, working travel-journal globe. Six locally loaded trips cover six continents; list, globe-marker, and clustered-marker selection all open synchronized trip details with highlighted locations. Filters, chronological view, empty-state recovery, reset-with-filter-preservation, shareable URL reload, and back navigation work. Valid real-time 3D is evident from the rotating globe's changing geography, marker occlusion, and spatial highlight changes. The 390px layout remains readable and exposes the controls, though keyboard activation and reduced-motion camera behavior were not directly exercised within the call budget.

runtime.reason: The page loaded at 1440x900 with the Meridian title, full interface, and WebGL globe. All application and photo resources in the network log returned 200; the only console error was a nonblocking missing favicon.ico (404).

scene.reason: The scene is a genuine interactive 3D globe rather than a static image: coastlines, lighting, surface shading, depth, and marker projections remain spatially coherent as the camera changes between Europe/Africa, Asia, and the Americas views.

checks.reason: Three distinct views show real depth and changing geometry: the initial Europe/Africa hemisphere, the Banff-focused Americas hemisphere, and a dragged Asia-centered view. Markers move with the sphere and far-side markers disappear behind it.

Composition, typography, color, and materials form a coherent editorial field-journal presentation. The cream archive panel, dark globe, green landmasses, and orange markers maintain clear hierarchy and legibility across desktop and mobile.

Primary UI actions produce meaningful feedback: selecting Kyoto from the list, Banff from its globe marker, and Lisbon from the nearby-trips popup each opened the corresponding article, updated the URL, and focused/highlighted the matching globe location.

Repeat and recovery flows work: combined search and year filtering reduced the archive to one result, a conflicting combination produced an explanatory empty state with a clear recovery action, timeline mode ordered trips newest to oldest, reset restored the full globe without clearing filters, and share/refresh/back navigation restored coherent journal context.

Desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844 layouts were inspected. The mobile full-page view keeps the globe, filter controls, all six trip entries, lower reset control, and footer content visible and readable. Reload preserved the direct trip URL. Network resources were healthy; the sole console issue was a nonblocking favicon 404.

The six-entry archive covers Europe, Asia, North America, Africa, Oceania, and South America. Each list entry exposes a locally bundled photo with meaningful alt text, specific dates, country, continent, and a diary summary; opened details for Kyoto, Banff, and Patagonia include full diary text and geographic coordinates. The network log confirms all six local JPEG assets loaded with 200 responses.

List and globe selection open the same journal context and matching highlight. Kyoto selected from the list opened Trip 02 and focused the Kyoto marker; Banff selected from its map marker opened Trip 03 and moved the globe to North America; the cluster-selected Lisbon opened Trip 01. Markers are placed consistently with the listed coordinates and continent.

Far-side trip markers are not exposed or selectable in the tested views; only markers on the visible hemisphere appear. The nearby Lisbon and Marrakech markers are disambiguated by a two-item popup, and each button independently selects its trip.

Search and year filters combine correctly, timeline mode is chronological (2025 to 2023), and zero matches produce a useful 'Nothing pinned here' explanation with a clear-search-and-year recovery action. After orbiting the camera with a lake/2024 filter active, Reset view restored the full globe while the active search and year remained unchanged.

A direct #trip=patagonia URL was loaded and reloaded; it restored Trip 06/06, the Patagonia article, coordinates, and map focus. Browser back returned to the root journal with all six journeys and Timeline mode still selected. The duplicate same-URL navigation used for the refresh required one extra back step but did not lose journal context.

All six trips are exposed as native buttons in the accessibility tree, and the 390px full-page layout is readable with ordinary document content below the globe and explicit vertical-scroll guidance on the canvas. However, actual Tab/Enter activation of every list item and the reduced-motion camera transition were not directly exercised within the call budget, so these aspects remain only partially verified.

instruction.reason: Core requested flows and content are delivered coherently, including trip synchronization, geographic placement, clustered markers, filtering, chronological view, empty-state recovery, reset behavior, shareable URLs, and back navigation. The score stops short of 4 because keyboard activation and reduced-motion camera handling were not directly verified.

spatial.reason: The globe consistently behaves as a sphere across multiple viewpoints. Continents and markers stay geographically coherent, near-side markers remain visible, far-side markers are occluded, and the selected location is highlighted without spatial contradictions.

interaction.reason: The primary flows, combinations, and recovery behavior are reliable: list and marker selection, cluster disambiguation, filtering, empty-state recovery, timeline switching, reset without filter loss, direct-trip reload, and back navigation all produced the expected visible state changes.

visual.reason: The distressed editorial typography, restrained cream and dark-green palette, map linework, photography, and orange pin accents consistently support the field-journal concept. Hierarchy remains clear in the desktop detail view, timeline, empty state, and mobile stacked layout.

stability.reason: Tested desktop, mobile, reload, filtering, selection, and history flows remained usable. Application and photo assets loaded successfully, but the console contains a nonblocking favicon 404, and one automated cluster-button click timed out because the animated marker was not stable while the camera settled.

limitations: The 40-call budget prevented a direct Tab/Enter pass through every trip button and an emulated prefers-reduced-motion camera-transition test; T06 is therefore marked PARTIAL.
Mobile evaluation used a 390x844 viewport rather than real touch hardware. The full-page render and scroll guidance confirm a scrollable document, but no physical touch gesture was performed.

Coordinates and full diary text were opened directly for Kyoto, Banff, and Patagonia; the other three entries were verified from list metadata, local photo assets, and consistently structured selection UI rather than individually opened detail panels.
No export/download control was present or advertised, so no downloaded-export flow applied.
Console and network diagnostics are recorded in evidence/console.txt and evidence/network.txt; they are not included in screenshot evidence arrays.
